headline: The FBI’s Springfield Field Office is now leading the investigation into an explosive device found at the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois. The FBI said it has confirmed an explosive device was found, and it’s working with ATF, Illinois State Police and local agencies to identify those responsible. According to authorities, Peoria Police were called to the facility just after 1 p.m. Friday. A suspicious device was located about 2 p.m. and deemed credible at 6:45 p.m. An evacuation of everyone within one mile followed just after 7 p.m. The device was rendered safe at 9:12 p.m. The search for additional devices continued until about 1 p.m. Saturday, when the order was lifted. No other devices were found. The evacuation lasted about 18 hours and affected thousands of people and spanned parts of downtown Peoria, the Warehouse District and East Peoria.

headline: The USS Spruance (DDG-111) and USS Michael Murphy (DDG-112) returned home this week after 357 and 346 day deployments, the latest sign of how the Navy has been stretched past its standard six to seven month deployments toward a year. Spruance’s deployment may be the longest by a destroyer since World War II. Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle told sailors to expect deployments of at least 10 months going forward, and Navy leaders told families of the USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77) carrier strike group to plan for a yearlong deployment if the blockade continues or the war restarts. Caudle also warned of a “years-long” recovery for the destroyer fleet’s maintenance backlog.

headline: U.S. intelligence analysts assess that Iran has between 1,500 and 2,500 missiles, U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal. It is a low confidence estimate because of the difficulty of tracking how many are ready for launch or in storage. Israeli military officials assess Iran has more than 1,500 ballistic missiles. The Journal says Iran also has many drones and short range missiles, and has kept building from stockpiled components, though more slowly than before the war. The Journal says the assessment stand in contrast to statements from administration officials, including President Donald J. Trump, that Iran’s military was decimated, and has informed internal discussions about resuming strikes. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said Tuesday that Iran’s defense industrial base is “gone.” A White House official said the U.S. campaign rendered Iranian forces “helpless.” The report follows Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) release of imagery November 10th of what they called a new underground “missile city,” showing the armed forces chief and the IRGC Aerospace Force commander touring tunnels with missiles and launchers.

headline: UN Secretary General Race: Where Things Stand The race to become the next UN Secretary General remains open after 8 informal Security Council straw polls. Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan holds a lead in Security Council voting and is now the clear favorite on Polymarket, with a 45% chance of winning. Current Polymarket odds: Rebeca Grynspan (Costa Rica): 45% Lana Nusseibeh (UAE): 21% Rafael Grossi (Argentina): 16.5% María Fernanda Espinosa (Ecuador): 6.8% Despite entering the race 3 weeks late, Nusseibeh remains a leading contender. To secure the position, a candidate needs at least 9 Security Council votes and no veto from any of the 5 permanent members. The next straw poll is tentatively scheduled for November 19. A consensus candidate, negotiated compromise or failure to select a successor by December 31 all remain possible.
